newsitem.title: USA: CBOT wheat ratchets to contract lows, export woes.
newsitem.headline: CBOT wheat ratchets to contract lows, export woes.

text.p: Huge fund selling and bearish export talk hammered CBOT wheat futures to a sharply lower close with nearby March and May ratcheting to new contract lows amid fast trading in late dealings, traders said.
"It was massive fund selling. Nearly every fund and commission house on the street sold it," said Paul Haugens, vice president for Chicago-based trade house FIMAT Futures.

Fund selling was estimated from 20 million to 30 million bushels. The contract low for March is $3.57 a bushel, down from the previous low of $3.63 set November 6. The new low for May is $3.47, down from the previous low of $3.48.
Fundamentals also remained suspect with India and Egypt central to the bearish export talk.
"There's potentially up to two million tonnes of business around here and the U.S. isn't going to get any of it. U.S. prices are too high," said FIMAT's wheat trading specialist Skip Searcy.
There was talk early this week that India and Egypt soon would be in the market respectively for 50,000 up to 750,000 tonnes and 400,000 to 800,000 tonnes.
Wheat closed two to 10-1/2 cents per bushel lower, with March down 10-1/2 at $3.59-3/4.
"There was the story Egypt and India are looking for wheat from other than the U.S.," said Ron Kucha of O'Connor and Co.

Traders said Prudential Securities and Rosenthal Collins each sold five million bushels of March, with Smith Barney, E.D. and F. Man International, Griffin Trading and Dean Witter each selling roughly three million bushels of March.
The wheat market also continued to struggle under the weight of large wheat stocks worldwide plus a more aggressive stance this week by the EU in offering export rebate wheat, they said.

World wheat production is set to jump again in 1997, after 1996's bumper crop, according to a leading monitoring organization. The London-based International Grains Council said the world crop in 1997 would total 585 million tonnes.
That's above the 580 million tonnes produced in 1996. The IGC pointed out that the back-to-back good crop years follow the drought-reduced crop in 1995 of 541 million tonnes.
Traders said weaker cash basis markets, especially in the U.S. hard red winter wheat region also weighed on wheat futures Friday.
"Cargill dropped their bids a couple of cents and there's a lack of business," a Kansas City trader said early Friday.
As of 1500 CST Friday, floor sources were estimating the total fund selling Friday in the wheat pit at 27 million bushels.
"There was tremendous fund selling in wheat late," said Vic Lespinasse of Dean Witter Reynolds.
Wheat futures volume was estimated by the CBOT at 16,000 contracts, sharply up from the 7,783 traded Thursday.
In wheat options, FIMAT Futures bought 400 March $3.70 calls at five to six cents, as well as buying 200 March $3.70 calls and 200 March $3.90 puts at 30 cents, traders said.
Wheat options volume was estimated at 8,000 contracts, up sharply from the 3,706 traded Thursday.
